## 1. Recipe sketch: adding a new top-level prose section (e.g., "Key takeaways")

The architecture is data-prep Python + `str.replace()` token substitution into a single template (`generate_results_viewer_v2.py:1370-1396`; design record: benchmarks README §8 "Template architecture"). Sections are static `<section>` scaffolds whose bodies are either hand-written prose (Hero, About) or empty `div.sec-body` containers filled by registered JS renderers.

**Steps, all in `/daaf/benchmarks/scripts/viewer_template.html` unless noted:**

1. **Section scaffold** — add `<section class="doc-section" id="key-takeaways">` with `<h2>` + `p.section-lead` in `<main class="doc">` (existing sections at L453–746). For a pure-prose section, write content directly (About pattern, L461–604: intro + `<details>` collapsibles); no `sec-body` div needed.
2. **TOC nav** — add `<a class="toc-link" href="#key-takeaways" data-target="key-takeaways">` in `nav#toc-rail` (L436–448).
3. **Scrollspy + lazy/deep-link registration** — add the id to `SECTION_IDS` (L2832); this drives scrollspy active state, IntersectionObserver lazy rendering, and `#hash` deep links (L3053–3064).
4. **If JS-rendered:** register a renderer in `sectionRenderers` (L2797–2805) and give the section a `div.sec-body` with id `sec-key-takeaways` (naming contract in `ensureRendered`, L2808–2813). Optionally add the id to the `content-visibility:auto` CSS rule (L78–85) with a plausible `contain-intrinsic-size`.
5. **If prose-with-computed-numbers (recommended for "Key takeaways"):** follow the existing two patterns —
   - **Span-injection (JS, About pattern):** prose contains `<span id="ab-runs">—</span>`; `fillAboutCounts()` (L1242–1269) fills spans from `PRECOMPUTED` at init. New computed numbers: compute in `build_precomputed()` (generator L919–1343), embed in the PRECOMPUTED bundle, fill spans in a new/extended fill function called from `init()` (L3013). This is the precomputed-headline pattern: "headline numbers are precomputed in Python and embedded so prose and charts cannot drift apart" (README §8).
   - **Generation-time placeholder (Python, `__GENERATED_DISPLAY__` pattern):** add a unique token in the template prose and a `html.replace("__TOKEN__", value)` line in `generate_html()` (L1392–1394). Substitution-order rule: small controlled placeholders first, `__DATA_JSON__` last so transcript content can never be treated as a placeholder (docstring L1376–1381). Note: README §8 writes the tokens as `/*__DATA_JSON__*/`, but in the template they are bare `const DATA = __DATA_JSON__;` / `const PRECOMPUTED = __PRECOMPUTED_JSON__;` (L754–755) — minor doc drift.
6. **Versioning** — bump `generator_version` (currently "2.5.0", generator L793). Output naming is automatic: dated auto-incrementing `viewer_YYYY-MM-DD{a,b,...}.html` in `benchmarks/` (L88–93), matching the framework's no-in-place-modification convention (README §8).
7. **Doc sync** — README §8 describes the section list ("single scrolling document (verdict, about, leaderboard, ...)" L584); update it.

For contrast, the *phase*-addition dev guide (generator L99–138) demands additional registries — `PHASE_MAP`, `PHASE_ORDER`/`EVAL_GROUP_ORDER`, `COMPOSITE_GIDS` (user approval required), `GROUP_SHORT` (template L945), `PD_EXPLAINERS` (L1769), the `order` array in buildEvalGroups (L935), `phaseSpan`/`ab-pX-cases` (L1259), About-table row (L514) — none of which apply to a prose-only section, but the guide is the model for documenting the new section's registration points.

## 2. Web-hosting gap list

Verified against `<head>` (L1–6) and full-template greps:

| Gap | Evidence | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| No `<meta name="description">` | head has only charset, viewport, title (L4–6) | trivial |
| No OpenGraph / Twitter card tags | grep `og:|twitter:` — zero matches | trivial (note: an OG image must be an absolute URL; either host one or omit) |
| No favicon | grep — zero matches; browsers will 404 `/favicon.ico` on the host | trivial (inline data-URI SVG keeps self-containment) |
| No canonical URL | absent | trivial |
| No print stylesheet | grep `@media print` — none; known deferred fast-follow (README §12 "Viewer fast-follows", L940) | moderate |
| Mobile: single breakpoint only | one `@media (max-width:900px)` collapsing the TOC rail (L92–103); wide tables/heatmaps/SVGs have no small-screen overflow treatment verified; hover tooltips (`showTip`, L1162) are mouse-only — touch UX unverified | moderate |
| 13.84 MB single-file payload on mobile | all data inline in two `<script>` constants (L754–755); render is lazy (content-visibility L78–85 + IntersectionObserver + idle queue L2789–2821) but **download+parse is not and cannot be lazy in a single file**; no gzip control in the artifact itself (host-level compression essential — JSON-heavy HTML should compress well) | structural (accepted consequence of the embedded-transcripts decision) |
| No-JS fallback | section bodies are empty divs filled by JS; a no-JS visitor sees headings/leads and "Rendering…" pseudo-content (L88–89); no `<noscript>` notice | trivial |
| Title is generic | `DAAF Benchmark Results` (L6) — fine, but worth aligning with public framing | trivial |
| A11y positives already present | `lang="en"` (L2), viewport meta (L5), h1→h2 hierarchy, colorblind-safe palette with glyph redundancy and ≥3:1 non-text contrast per design record (README §8 "Design system"; tokens L13–29) | — |
| A11y unverified | heatmaps/SVG charts are presentational markup; no aria labels found by inspection of read regions; keyboard operability of click-handlers (`onclick` deep-links) unverified | moderate (audit needed) |

**External requests: confirmed zero.** Grep for `https?://|src=|fetch(|@import|url(` in the template — no matches. Inline SVG, zero chart libraries (README §8).

## 3. file:// vs. http(s) behavioral differences to retest

Single switch: `var isFileProto=(location.protocol==="file:")` (template L1126). Differences:

- **Explicit navigation hash writes** (`setHash`, L1128–1138): `location.hash` on file:// (Chrome restricts `history.replaceState` there); `history.replaceState` on http(s), with `location.hash` fallback in catch. Retest deep links `#section` and `#run-explorer&run=<dir>` (parseHash L1140–1150) under https.
- **Scrollspy hash writes** (L2844–2846): writes nothing on file://; on http(s) it continuously `history.replaceState`s the hash during scroll — first time this branch is the live path for real users. Retest: back-button behavior, scroll-jump absence, and shared-URL accuracy.
- **content-visibility + hash navigation** (CSS comment L69–77): engine renders the navigation target on jump "(Chrome / Firefox 125+)" — retest anchor accuracy over http on Chrome/Firefox/Safari.
- Host-level additions to verify: gzip/brotli on a 13.84 MB response, any CSP the site applies (the page is one giant inline script — `script-src 'unsafe-inline'` or hash-based CSP required), and MIME/charset headers.

## 5. Publishing-workflow observations

- **The artifact lives outside the repo.** `viewer_*.html` is gitignored (`/daaf/benchmarks/.gitignore:18`), with the template explicitly re-included (`!scripts/viewer_template.html`, L20). Rationale: "contains embedded result data" — and `results/` itself is gitignored (L3), so a fresh clone **cannot regenerate the viewer**; the publishable HTML exists only on the maintainer's machine (`viewer_2026-06-11d.html` is current, README §12 L1015).
- **No deploy tooling exists in the repo.** Repo-wide grep for deploy/netlify/vercel/gh-pages/cloudflare/publish found nothing relevant; glob `**/*deploy*` matches only a marimo skill reference. The website (daaf.openaugments.org) is maintained outside this repo — a prior search-agent had to *web-fetch* the live site to extract its content (`/daaf/research/2026-06-10_FrameworkDev_UserDoc02Sync/preliminary_notes/2026-06-10_website_verbatim_extraction.md`). Publishing is therefore a manual out-of-band step: generate locally → upload to wherever the site is hosted. Any "deploy" recipe will need user-supplied hosting mechanics.
- Auto-increment naming means each regeneration is a new file; a public deployment will want a stable URL (e.g., upload-as-`benchmarks.html` or symlink at the host) — currently no convention for that. Old viewer retention/deletion is pending user housekeeping (README §12 L1021–1023).
